Architecture Diagram

PhotoGallery is a single ASP.NET MVC web application that serves a Razor UI and uses Azure Blob Storage for photo persistence. No database or independently deployable backend service was identified.

Data Storage & External Services

Photo files are stored in an Azure Blob Storage container. The application does not define a relational database, cache, message broker, or other external API. The configured local default is the development storage emulator.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The MVC controller combines request handling with Azure storage operations; no separate service or repository layer is present.
  • Photo metadata is obtained from the blob listing rather than a separate application database.
  • The container is created with public blob read access.

The application exposes four MVC actions through browser-oriented HTTP requests and has no separate service-to-service API. Requests are synchronous at the application boundary, with asynchronous blob upload and deletion calls to Azure Storage.

DTOs & Contracts

The application does not define request or response DTO classes. MVC binds uploaded content through Request.Files; gallery view data is a list of blob URIs. The Azure SDK supplies blob metadata types. No OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL contracts were found.

Communication Patterns

The browser communicates with the MVC application over HTTP. The controller directly calls Azure Blob Storage using the Azure SDK for listing, uploading, and deleting. No message broker, service discovery, API gateway, retry policy, circuit breaker, or explicit timeout policy was identified. The application code does not configure API authentication or authorization, and it enables public blob reads when creating the container. TLS for storage is provided by the external Azure endpoint; no application-level HTTPS enforcement was identified.

Core Business Workflows

PhotoGallery lets users browse a gallery of photos stored as blobs, upload additional photos, and delete one or all stored photos. The primary business data is the photo content and its public blob URI.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
PhotoBlobPhoto GalleryAn uploaded image or other file stored in the blob containerBelongs to the gallery container

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
WebApp-Storage-DotNetPhoto GalleryGallery operations and photo selectionAzure Blob Storage
Azure Blob StorageObject StorageStored photo blobsNone identified

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the Photo Gallery

  1. A visitor opens the gallery page.
  2. The controller creates the storage client and ensures the gallery container exists.
  3. The application lists block blobs, collects their URIs, and renders the gallery.
  4. If storage access fails, an error view is returned.

Workflow 2: Upload Photos

  1. A visitor selects one or more files and submits the multipart form.
  2. The controller creates a generated blob name using a timestamp, GUID, and uploaded file extension.
  3. The content is uploaded to Azure Blob Storage and the visitor is redirected to the gallery.
  4. No server-side file-type or business validation is identified.

Workflow 3: Delete Photos

The visitor can submit a delete request for one displayed blob URI or request deletion of all block blobs. The controller resolves the blob name and calls the storage delete operation, then redirects to the gallery.

Cross-Service Data Flows

The MVC application directly calls Azure Blob Storage. Blob names and URIs returned by storage are used to render the photo gallery. There are no additional services or response-composition flows. If storage is unavailable, the application displays an error rather than providing a cached or partial gallery.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Visitor participant Gallery as "PhotoGallery" participant Storage as "Azure Blob Storage" Visitor->>Gallery: Open gallery Gallery->>Storage: List photo blobs Storage-->>Gallery: Blob metadata and URIs Gallery-->>Visitor: Display photos Visitor->>Gallery: Submit selected photo files Gallery->>Gallery: Generate unique blob names Gallery->>Storage: Upload photo blobs Storage-->>Gallery: Upload result Gallery-->>Visitor: Redirect to gallery Visitor->>Gallery: Request single or bulk deletion Gallery->>Storage: Delete target blob or all blobs Storage-->>Gallery: Delete result Gallery-->>Visitor: Redirect to gallery

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Only block blobs are displayed and selected for bulk deletion.
  • A new blob name combines the current timestamp, a GUID, and the original file extension.
  • Single-photo deletion extracts the final path component from the submitted URI before selecting the blob to delete.
  • The application has no identified user authentication, ownership checks, or audit trail for uploads and deletions.
  • No explicit transaction or compensating-action workflow is present; each blob operation is performed directly against storage.

No application cache, cache provider, or cache policy was identified. The controller retrieves blob listings from storage when rendering the gallery.

Data Ownership Boundaries

Photo content is owned by a single Azure Storage container. There is no shared database, database-per-service topology, cross-service query, CQRS flow, or application-level aggregation. The application directly lists and mutates the container.
